fields.meta_title: Insurance Landing Page for Quotes and Callbacks | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See how four agencies handle auto quotes, life callbacks, business requests, and renewal reviews on an insurance landing page. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Insurance Landing Page That Routes Every Quote
fields.hero_description: Build an insurance landing page that sends each quote request to the right agent and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Six Parts of an Insurance Quote Page
fields.features_subheading: Each part moves a visitor from an ad click to a request an agent can quote, and Emergent changes any of them when you prompt it.
fields.feature_1:
A coverage question before the name

Open the form with fixed choices: Auto, Home, Life, or Business. The pick decides which agent hears about the request, so place it above the name and phone number fields.
fields.feature_2:
Four fields, then the button

Ask for the name, phone number, ZIP code, and coverage line, then stop. Vehicle numbers and prior claims can wait for the agent's call, where people explain them in their own words.
fields.feature_3:
Every request saved with its line

Each request lands in a database you own with its coverage line and the minute it arrived. Agents work the list from the top and mark each row Quoted or Not a fit once they call.
fields.feature_4:
An email to the agent who writes that line

Send Auto requests to one agent and Life requests to another by email, or post each one to the Slack channel. The alert carries the visitor's number and the coverage they picked.
fields.feature_5:
Requests passed on to your CRM

The page can send each request to the agency system or CRM you already use, through that tool's API. Agents then quote from the record they open every day, not a separate inbox.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Export the page's full code to a GitHub repository on paid plans, or keep publishing the finished page from Emergent. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

fields.tab_content_1:
Auto quotes go to Ewan, not the front desk

Tern River Insurance asks which of its four coverage lines a visitor wants before anything else. Every Auto pick sends an email to Ewan Vann, the agent who writes auto, with the visitor's number in it. This week 34 quote requests came in: 19 picked Auto, and 15 went to the front desk.
fields.tab_content_2:
No cold calls: 6 of 14 picked Evening

Bridgemont Life stopped calling people at dinner. Its page asks when to call back: Morning, Afternoon, or Evening. Each request is saved with its window, and the agent's call list for the day is sorted by it. Today 14 people asked for a callback: 6 picked Evening, 5 picked Morning, and 3 picked Afternoon.
fields.tab_content_3:
From 10 employees up, Verity takes the call

Stonecrow Commercial asks how many people a business employs. A business with 10 or more employees goes to Verity Lantram, the commercial lines producer, and a smaller one books a 15-minute call with the next open agent. This month 27 requests came in: 9 went to Verity, and 18 booked the call.
fields.tab_content_4:
Reviews run 30 minutes after a life change

Alder Gate Agency emails clients a review page before renewal that asks whether anything changed this year. A client who ticks Something changed books a 30-minute review, and everyone else books 15 minutes. In October 40 clients booked: 12 ticked Something changed, and 28 booked the shorter slot.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Insurance Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an insurance landing page that asks the right first question and gets each quote request to the agent who writes it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Point each ad at the page for its line
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Say who calls back and when
fields.howto_step_1_des: Give auto and life their own pages, and send each ad to the page for its line. Google Ads counts the quality of your ads and landing page in Ad Rank, including the expectations users have about your landing page based on the clicked ad creative.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Label each choice with the words your ads use. A visitor who clicked a life insurance ad should see Life on the first screen. List only the lines the agency writes, because a line nobody quotes has no place on the form.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Under the button, say who calls back and the hours the phones are answered, such as weekdays from 8 am to 6 pm. A visitor who submits at 9 pm then knows the call comes the next morning, not in five minutes.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Google uses the mobile version of a site's content, crawled with the smartphone agent, for indexing and ranking. Review that layout before the desktop one: the coverage choices should fit on one screen, and the phone number should be a button a thumb can tap.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Let the visitor pick one of three windows instead of waiting for a call at a random hour. Print the hours behind each window on the page, such as Evening for 5 pm to 8 pm. The agent and the visitor then read it the same way.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Name the agent for each line
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write down who hears about each request before you build: Auto to one agent, commercial to a producer, everything else to the front desk. Name a backup for each line, for the days its agent is out. No request should wait in an inbox nobody reads.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it and send a test quote
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the coverage lines and the agent for each one, and Emergent builds the page and its database from that prompt. Submit a test quote from a phone, then check the new row and the email that reached the agent.

faq_plan.q: What is an insurance landing page?
faq_plan.a: An insurance landing page is a single web page that asks a visitor to request one kind of coverage quote, such as auto or life, or to book a call with an agent. It has no site menu: the only ways forward are the quote form and the phone number.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an insurance landing page?
faq_plan.a: Pick the coverage line the page quotes and the agent who answers it, then describe both to Emergent's AI landing page builder. Emergent builds the page and the database behind its quote form from that prompt, and you change any part by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: Is an insurance landing page template enough to get quote requests?
faq_plan.a: Not on its own. A template gives you the layout: a headline and a form block. It does not know which lines you write or who should get each request. You still connect the form to an inbox or a CRM yourself. When Emergent builds the page from a prompt, the routing logic and the database come with it.

faq_plan.q: Can one insurance landing page also advertise home loans?
faq_plan.a: It is better not to. Give each offer its own page, because each one asks different questions. A home insurance quote asks about the property and the coverage wanted, while a mortgage landing page asks about the loan amount and the buyer's timeline. Link the two pages to each other if the agency refers clients both ways.

faq_plan.q: How do I see which ad brought in each lead on an insurance landing page?
faq_plan.a: Add a hidden field that saves the campaign tag from the ad's link with every request. Count requests by tag at the end of each week, and move spend toward the ads that bring in the lines you want to write. On a page Emergent builds, the tag sits in the same database row as the request.

faq_plan.q: How many insurance landing pages does an agency need?
faq_plan.a: Start with one page for each coverage line you advertise, plus one for clients coming up for renewal. Add another page only when a campaign needs an offer the existing pages do not carry, such as coverage for restaurant owners.

faq_plan.q: Should an insurance landing page include a video?
faq_plan.a: It can, if the clip answers a question the form raises, such as a 60-second intro from the agent who will call back. Place it beside or below the form, never in front of it. A page built around the clip itself is a video landing page, which calls for a different layout.

faq_plan.q: Can an insurance landing page send quote requests to my CRM?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A page Emergent builds connects to any tool with an API and sends each request in as a new record. Map each form field to its CRM field before launch, then send one test request to confirm the coverage line lands in the right place.

faq_plan.q: What headline works on an insurance landing page?
faq_plan.a: Name the coverage and the next step in the visitor's words, such as an auto insurance quote by tomorrow morning. Match the headline to the ad that sent the visitor there, and leave rates out of it unless the page can show a quote that matches.

faq_plan.q: How is a health insurance landing page different from an auto one?
faq_plan.a: A health insurance page asks about the household and the ZIP code instead of a vehicle, and it leaves medical details for the agent's call. A care provider's page, such as a mental health landing page, books appointments, while a health insurance page books a talk about plans.

plan.angle: Searchers for insurance landing page get template galleries (Pinterest, Figma, a theme shop), a 2021 design guide and an old list of life insurance pages: all of them show how a page looks, none shows what happens to a quote request after the visitor submits it. This page shows four agency pages built around that hand-off (an auto quote that emails the auto agent, a life insurance callback the visitor schedules, a business request sorted by headcount, a renewal review that gets longer when something changed), each with its form, its routing and its database row, then gives the build steps. It makes no claims about insurance law, licensing, rates or consent wording. The mortgage page is a sibling and stays out of the headings.
